title: QBR triage scenario lab notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working QBR-focused triage lab for accounts showing early-to-mid stage renewal risk. The goal: give CSMs an actionable, repeatable checklist they can run in the 72-hour window after a negative signal, plus a compact set of "save plays" mapped to root causes and a short exec-escalation script for the CRO/GM to use.

Status notes: draft -> running through two pilot accounts this quarter (Nov/Dec) then iterate. Use this doc as a mutable playbook during QBR prep; capture outcomes in JIRA ticket and postmortem in /confluence.

How to use:
- Run the triage checklist immediately on signal ingestion (automated or manual). Target: complete within 72 hours.
- Score the account using the attached rubric (below). If score >= 7/10 raise to "priority save" and book play pairing meeting within 48 hours.
- Use the short email templates to coordinate internal stakeholders, then prepare the QBR agenda that centers the save hypothesis and success metrics.

Quick triage checklist (72-hour):
1) Validate signal origin: billing churn notice / support surge / latency/regression alert / product usage drop / competitive mention. Note timestamps and ticket/alert ids.
2) Customer health snapshot: last 30/90/365 day token consumption, average latency, error-rate, feature usage map. Export as CSV and attach to JIRA.
3) Customer sentiment: recent PL/SE notes, CSAT/CS feedback, support SLA misses, exec comms.
4) Contract state: renewal window, auto-renew clauses, committed spend, active purchase orders, billing disputes.
5) Dependencies: Are there integrations or internal vendor blockers? Any private deployment (VPC) that complicates fixes?
6) Risk owner and observers: assign CSM (owner), AM, Solutions Eng, Product Reliability contact. Add exec sponsor if score >= 7.
7) Timeboxed mitigation hypothesis: 3 action items with owners and 7-day checkpoints.

Signal scoring rubric (0–10):
- Usage drop (0–3): 0 = stable, 1 = minor dip (<15%), 2 = sustained dip (15–40%), 3 = steep drop (>40%) or complete stop
- Product regressions (0–2): 0 = none, 1 = intermittent errors or latency spikes, 2 = production regression causing failures or major quality issues
- Commercial pressure (0–2): 0 = none, 1 = pricing concern surfaced, 2 = competitive RFP / procurement push
- Exec engagement (0–2): 0 = highly engaged, 1 = neutral, 2 = disengaged or asking for alternatives
Interpretation: 0–3 low risk, 4–6 medium risk, 7–10 high risk (priority save).

Root-cause categories and paired save plays (concise):
A) Usage drop due to value gap
  - Diagnosis: low feature adoption, no internal champion, mismatched integration.
  - Save plays: rapid value workshop (SE-led) within 7 days, co-developed success metrics, 30-day pilot with custom prompts and ROI tracking.
  - Success metric: +20% active model invocations week-over-week in pilot.

B) Product quality/regression
  - Diagnosis: model regressions, increased hallucinations, latency regressions after deployment.
  - Save plays: immediate rollback to last-good model, enable degraded-mode routing (fallback model variant), SE-led remediation runbook + hotfix SLA.
  - Success metric: error-rate <1% and median latency within SLO within 48 hours.

C) Commercial / pricing friction
  - Diagnosis: pricing pushed by procurement, surprise overages, unclear cost breakdowns.
  - Save plays: arrange CFO-to-CFO cost walkthrough, propose short-term concession (credits or temporary rate), present Optimize report showing cost reduction levers (batching / quantization / KV caching).
  - Success metric: signed commitment to renewed PO terms within the next billing cycle or formal extension agreement.

D) Security/compliance blocker (private deployments)
  - Diagnosis: audit findings, KMS/HSM concerns, network/VPC constraints.
  - Save plays: escalate to Security & Private Deployments lead, propose snapshot remediation plan, offer timeboxed managed deployment support and audit liaison.
  - Success metric: remediation plan accepted and timeline aligned with renewal milestone.

Priority save playbook (for score >= 7):
Phase 0 (0–48h): assemble rapid response pod: CSM owner, AM, Solutions Eng, SRE on-call, Product PM, Security if relevant. Kickoff with customer: "We want to remove obstacles this week — here are 3 concrete actions we will take and the dates."
Phase 1 (3–14 days): execute the three actions (pilot, rollback/hotfix, commercial concession), run daily 15-min sync with customer and internal pod. Capture runbook tasks in JIRA and link to QBR notes.
Phase 2 (15–30 days): confirm signal reversal via agreed metrics; prepare executive summary for QBR and either transition to renewal play or continue escalation to exec sponsor.

Exec escalation: short script and outcomes
- When to escalate: risk score >= 8, or 6–7 with imminent contract expiration (<30 days) and no remediation progress within 7 days.
- Exec script (CRO -> Customer exec): "We value our partnership and want to ensure your team gets predictable value from Redwood. We've assembled a response pod and propose X, Y, Z as concrete steps. I'd like your feedback and a short alignment call to confirm priority and timeline."
- Desired outcomes: visible exec alignment, resource commitment (customer and Redwood), and a formalized extension or decision timeline.

QBR agenda template (30–60 minutes, pivoted for a recovery QBR):
- 5 min: Purpose and desired decision outcome for meeting (what success looks like)
- 10 min: Data presentation — usage, error-rate, latency, cost
  - key slide: trending tokens/day, top endpoints by volume, error-rate trend, cost attribution table (model+region)
- 10 min: Customer perspective — pain points, blockers, procurement signals
- 10 min: Proposed remediation plan (3 items) with owners and dates
- 5 min: Exec ask and next steps (commitment / follow-up cadence)

Internal RACI snippet (editable):
- CSM: owner of diagnosis, primary customer communication, drive QBR agenda
- Solutions Eng: technical remediation and pilot work
- SRE/Infra: rollback/hotfix and latency investigation
- Product PM: product-level root cause and roadmap inputs
- Sales/AM: commercial concessions and contract negotiation
- CRO/GM: final exec escalation and sponsor alignment

Templates (quick copy/paste)
Internal slack ping to pod:
"CSM-Rapid: account ACME (acct-123) flagged by usage drop (–55% last 14d). Triage complete, risk score 8/10. Need SE for pilot, SRE for rollback prep, AM for PO check. Kickoff in 1 hour. Notes and JIRA: JIRA-4521."

Customer email (to align for QBR recovery)
Subject: Quick alignment: next steps to stabilize usage and renew partnership
Hi <Name>,
Thanks for the candid feedback this month. We want to make sure Redwood is delivering predictable value. We've put together a focused 3-step plan to stabilize your environment and demonstrate consistent value in the next 30 days. Can we book a 30–45 min QBR recovery meeting this week to walk through the data and agree next steps?
Best,
<CSM name>

Data exports to attach to ticket (minimum):
- 30/90 day usage CSV (tokens, calls, endpoints)
- Top 10 error/ticket IDs and timestamps
- Latency percentiles by region/model
- Cost breakdown last 90 days (model, region, route)

Pilot checklist (if play includes a timeboxed pilot):
- Define success metric and measurement method (owner + query)
- Baseline current values before pilot start
- Define pilot cohort and scoped prompts or endpoints
- Put rollback criteria in writing and timebox the pilot
- Weekly checkpoint deliverables for customer and execs

Notes / open questions (working):
- How do we automate risk scoring from telemetry? (SE infra ticket)
- Can Console surface a "request save play" button that creates the triage JIRA and assigns pod automatically? (product-ops)
- Need a short internal training deck (10 slides) for AMs and CSMs that covers the rubric and playbook flow — assign to solutions enablement.

Pilot outcomes to capture in postmortem template:
- hypothesis, actions taken, metric deltas, timeline, decision (renew, extend, churn), lessons learned and playbook changes.

Appendix: sample compact metrics table (copy/paste into QBR slide)
Account | 30d tokens | 90d tokens | Avg latency p50/ms | Error-rate % | Risk score
ACME   | 18,200    | 120,430   | 310                | 3.8         | 8
BetaCo | 92,000    | 300,000   | 120                | 0.2         | 2

Finish: keep this doc lean and actionable. Replace with final consolidated playbook after two pilots and cross-functional review. If you add a new play, please annotate the date and pilot outcomes in the header.
